identification.summary: Nylon Typhoon (formerly NICKEL) is a China-based espionage actor that Microsoft says targets governments, diplomatic entities and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) across Central and South America, the Caribbean, Europe and North America [S1][S4]. MITRE ATT&CK tracks the same group as Ke3chang (G0004), attributed to actors operating out of China, which has targeted oil, government, diplomatic, military and NGO organizations since at least 2010 [S3]. Microsoft reports that the actor achieved long-term access to several victims and ran regularly scheduled data exfiltration [S1].
identification.firstObserved: MITRE: targeting since at least 2010 [S3]. Microsoft has tracked NICKEL since 2016 and tracked the operations it disclosed in 2021 since September 2019 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Nylon Typhoon (formerly NICKEL). Microsoft maps NICKEL, VIXEN PANDA, Playful Dragon, RedRiver, ke3chang, APT15 and Mirage to it [S4]. In 2021 Microsoft wrote that it 'observed some common activity' with actors known as APT15, APT25 and KeChang, which is an overlap statement rather than a one-to-one equivalence [S1]. MITRE lists Ke3chang, APT15, Mirage, Vixen Panda, GREF, Playful Dragon, RoyalAPT, NICKEL and Nylon Typhoon as associated names [S3]. The imported summary on this record described ESET's 'GREF' cluster (active since March 2017, Android BadBazaar campaigns against Uyghurs). That summary was not carried forward because no source gathered here ties that ESET cluster to Microsoft's Nylon Typhoon (see gaps).

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China (state nexus). Microsoft describes NICKEL as a China-based threat actor [S1][S4], and MITRE attributes Ke3chang to actors operating out of China [S3]. None of the sources gathered names a specific PRC agency or unit.
attribution.confidence: Microsoft attributes the activity to NICKEL / Nylon Typhoon by name and assesses that China-based actors will keep targeting government, diplomatic and NGO sectors, likely for economic espionage or traditional intelligence collection [S1]. Microsoft did not publish a numeric or worded confidence level for state sponsorship. The December 2021 domain seizure was a civil action by Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit under a US District Court order, not a US government attribution [S1][S2].
attribution.basis: Microsoft MSTIC telemetry and customer notifications, plus the DCU seizure of NICKEL-operated websites [S1][S2]; sign-in activity concentrated Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00 China Standard Time [S1]; long-running vendor reporting summarized by MITRE ATT&CK (Mandiant, NCC Group, Intezer, ESET) [S3][S6][S7][S8][S9]; Mandiant reporting on shared China-nexus ORB infrastructure [S5].

objectives: Intelligence collection against foreign ministries, diplomatic entities, other government bodies and NGOs. Microsoft assesses this is likely in pursuit of economic espionage or traditional intelligence collection as China expands bilateral relations and Belt and Road partnerships [S1]. Mandiant's 2014 Operation Ke3chang report focused on attacks against Ministries of Foreign Affairs [S3][S9].

sectors: Government, including ministries of foreign affairs [S1][S9]
regions: Central and South America, with a large share of activity against Central and South American governments [S1]
North America, including the United States [S1][S3]
Africa: Mali appears among the 29 countries Microsoft listed [S1]
Middle East: Mandiant lists it among regions historically targeted by APT15 and APT5 via SPACEHOP [S5]
targeting.notes: Microsoft's December 2021 list of 29 targeted countries: Argentina, Barbados, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Bulgaria, Chile, Colombia, Croatia, Czech Republic, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, France, Guatemala, Honduras, Hungary, Italy, Jamaica, Mali, Mexico, Montenegro, Panama, Peru, Portugal, Switzerland, Trinidad and Tobago, United Kingdom, United States and Venezuela [S1]. In its 2021 Digital Defense Report summary, Microsoft names NICKEL among the four nation-state groups most active against the government sector from July 2020 to June 2021, mostly against government entities involved in international affairs [S10].

capabilities.summary: Initial access through exploits against unpatched internet-facing Microsoft Exchange and SharePoint servers and remote-access appliances such as VPNs, including a Pulse Secure VPN vulnerability [S1]. MITRE also records VPN access using compromised accounts and stolen VPN certificates [S3][S6]. Credential theft uses keyloggers, Mimikatz, WDigest abuse and NTDSDump [S1]. Custom backdoors include Neoichor, Leeson, NumbIdea, NullItch and Rokum; several use the Internet Explorer COM interface for C2 hidden in legitimate-looking web pages, and implants are dropped into existing application paths to blend in [S1]. Stolen credentials are used for routine Microsoft 365 email collection through browser sign-ins and legacy Exchange Web Services, routed through commercial VPNs and actor infrastructure [S1]. Scheduled, incremental file collection is staged and archived with renamed RAR or 7-Zip [S1]. Earlier tooling includes RoyalCLI and RoyalDNS (DNS C2) and the SharePoint dumping tool spwebmember [S3][S6], the MirageFox RAT, an upgraded Mirage [S3][S7], and the Okrum backdoor, in use since December 2016 [S3][S8]. Mandiant reports that APT15 has used the provisioned ORB network SPACEHOP for reconnaissance scanning and vulnerability exploitation [S5].

campaigns.name: Operation Ke3chang (Mandiant)
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reported targeted attacks against Ministries of Foreign Affairs, including spearphishing attachments disguised with the right-to-left override character (as summarized by MITRE).

campaigns.name: Okrum and Ketrican backdoors (ESET)
campaigns.summary: ESET's July 2019 report describes Okrum, a Windows backdoor in use since December 2016 with strong links to Ke3chang (as summarized by MITRE).

campaigns.name: RoyalCLI and RoyalDNS intrusion (NCC Group)
campaigns.summary: NCC Group reported APT15 activity using the RoyalCLI and RoyalDNS backdoors, Exchange mailbox dumping with compromised credentials, VPN access with stolen certificates and spwebmember SharePoint dumping (as summarized by MITRE).

campaigns.name: MirageFox (Intezer)
campaigns.summary: Intezer reported MirageFox, an upgraded version of the Mirage RAT attributed to APT15 (as summarized by MITRE).

campaigns.name: NICKEL operations against Latin American and European governments
campaigns.summary: Microsoft tracked NICKEL attacks against government, diplomatic and NGO targets in 29 countries from September 2019. The actor exploited Exchange, SharePoint and VPN flaws, used custom backdoors and collected email through Microsoft 365.

campaigns.name: Use of SPACEHOP (ORB3) relay network
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reports that the SPACEHOP provisioned ORB network, active since at least 2019, supported reconnaissance and exploitation by China-nexus actors including APT15. MITRE tracks this as campaign C0052.

campaigns.name: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2021
campaigns.summary: Microsoft names NICKEL among the nation-state groups most active against the government sector from July 2020 to June 2021.

campaigns.name: Microsoft DCU seizure of NICKEL websites
campaigns.summary: Under a court order from the US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit seized a set of NICKEL-operated websites to disrupt attacks on organizations in 29 countries.

diamond.adversary: China-based espionage operators that Microsoft tracks as Nylon Typhoon (NICKEL) [S1][S4]. Sign-in activity clusters on weekdays from 08:00 to 17:00 China Standard Time, with possible shift-based scheduling [S1].
diamond.capability: Exploits for Exchange, SharePoint and VPN appliances. Credential theft with Mimikatz, WDigest, NTDSDump and keyloggers. Custom backdoors Neoichor, Leeson, NumbIdea, NullItch and Rokum [S1]. Legacy tools RoyalCLI, RoyalDNS, MirageFox and Okrum [S3][S6][S7][S8].
diamond.infrastructure: Actor-operated websites used for C2, seized by Microsoft DCU in 2021 [S1][S2]. Hardcoded C2 servers return legitimate-looking HTML that hides Base64 shellcode [S1]. Commercial VPN providers carry account sign-ins [S1]. The SPACEHOP ORB network uses leased VPS nodes, with relay servers in China or Hong Kong [S5]. RoyalDNS used DNS for C2 [S3].
diamond.victim: Foreign ministries and other government bodies, diplomatic entities and NGOs in Latin America, the Caribbean, Europe, North America and Mali [S1]. MITRE adds oil and military targets [S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Microsoft links the targeting to China's growing global influence, its bilateral relations and Belt and Road partnerships, with likely economic-espionage or traditional intelligence-collection aims [S1].
diamond.technology: Unpatched on-premises Exchange and SharePoint, remote-access VPN appliances, Microsoft 365 accounts reachable through legacy authentication (EWS), and Windows hosts where credentials are cached in memory [S1].

gaps: No public Microsoft reporting dated after 2021 specifically on Nylon Typhoon was found. Activity since the December 2021 seizure is undocumented in the sources gathered, apart from Mandiant's 2024 mention of APT15 using SPACEHOP [S5].
Microsoft's DCU announcement and the court filings (S2) could not be opened. Seizure details come from the MSTIC blog [S1].

Primary reports were not opened because their hosts were blocked: Mandiant Operation Ke3chang (2014), NCC Group RoyalCLI/RoyalDNS (2018), Intezer MirageFox (2018), ESET Okrum and Ketrican (2019), and Palo Alto Unit 42 TidePool. Their content is used only as summarized by MITRE ATT&CK.

Cluster boundary: ESET's 'GREF' (active since March 2017; Android BadBazaar trojanized Signal and Telegram apps targeting Uyghurs) appears in the imported summary, and MISP lists it as a separate entry from APT15. MITRE's GREF alias rests on older NCC Group reporting [S3]. No source gathered here establishes that ESET's GREF mobile activity belongs to Microsoft's Nylon Typhoon, so it is excluded.

Microsoft stated only 'common activity' with APT15, APT25 and KeChang in 2021 [S1]. APT25 is not in Microsoft's current Nylon Typhoon mapping [S4]. The exact boundary with Mandiant's APT15 and APT25 is unresolved.

Secureworks BRONZE PALACE, BRONZE DAVENPORT and BRONZE IDLEWOOD, plus the aliases Lurid, Metushy, Red Vulture, Social Network Team and Royal APT, are unverified. The Secureworks profile could not be opened.
No specific PRC sponsoring agency (MSS, PLA or contractor) and no US government indictment or advisory naming this actor was found.

Google Threat Intelligence's APT15 profile (sectors: trade, economic and financial, energy, military; ENFAL, BALDEAGLE, NOISEMAKER and MIRAGE malware) was read but carries no publication date, so it is not cited.
The Microsoft mapping file (S4) is a living document. Its date is the access date, not a publication date.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (define the OE): Key cyber terrain is internet-facing Exchange, SharePoint and VPN appliances, plus Microsoft 365 tenants that still allow legacy authentication (EWS). It matters most for foreign-affairs, diplomatic and partner-nation government networks in Latin America, the Caribbean, Europe and North America [S1]. STEP 2 (describe effects): Exposed and unpatched remote-access edges are the entry point. Shared ORB relay networks such as SPACEHOP spread source infrastructure across commercial VPS providers, which weakens IP-based blocking and attribution [S1][S5]. STEP 3 (adversary template): Exploit edge service or VPN, then dump credentials (Mimikatz, NTDSDump, WDigest, keylogger), then deploy an IE-COM backdoor in a legitimate software path, then collect mailboxes through M365/EWS sign-ins over commercial VPNs, then run recurring, date-filtered file collection archived with renamed RAR or 7-Zip [S1]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is quiet, long-term diplomatic and government intelligence collection with scheduled exfiltration from partner-nation ministries [S1]. MDCOA is persistent access to partner-nation foreign-affairs and military networks, or to shared coalition email, exposing coalition planning or negotiating positions (analyst extrapolation from the targeting [S1][S3]). Candidate indicators: EWS or legacy-auth sign-ins from commercial VPN ranges during 00:00-09:00 UTC on weekdays; WDigest UseLogonCredential being enabled; executables such as AcroRd64.exe or FoxitRdr64.exe in unexpected application folders; IE registry changes (IEHarden=0, ClearBrowsingHistoryOnExit=1); renamed rar.exe or 7z.exe with keyboard-walk passwords [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: Fuse identity telemetry (legacy-auth and EWS sign-ins, VPN-sourced logons) with edge-device patch status. The actor relies on valid credentials after initial exploitation, so host-only sensing will miss mailbox collection [S1]. Track ORB/SPACEHOP-linked infrastructure as shared China-nexus terrain rather than as a single-actor indicator [S5]. Authorities: The 2021 disruption came through a private civil seizure (Microsoft DCU under a US District Court order), not government action [S1][S2]. Planners should not count such actions as DoD effects, and they should coordinate deconfliction with private-sector disruption efforts. Mission assurance: Block legacy authentication, enforce MFA, apply the ASR rule against LSASS credential theft, and prioritize patching of Exchange, SharePoint and VPN appliances on DODIN and mission-partner enclaves [S1]. Coordination: Many victims are partner-nation and Western Hemisphere foreign ministries [S1]. Information sharing with partner nations and combatant commands, especially SOUTHCOM-area partners, is an analyst-inferred coordination need for protecting shared diplomatic and military communications.
